meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's zero entered before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did anyone ask Owen about any of this before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. I'll want those times in an email. What else do you have besides this?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote from memory all the time. That's a bad quotation, not proof of anything.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. Whatever you think this is, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is there anything else on that laptop?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's what drafting is.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Fine. I'll agree to the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The zero comes off the gradebook tonight, with the writing, and my questions about who decided go in my email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth, after school. I'll confirm with Owen tonight. Put the time and room in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday, November 12, after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, the time and room confirmed in writing, and an answer to who decided on the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen first. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook, the details in writing tonight, and an answer on who decided; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You showed that the quotation in the essay appears nowhere in the scene and then answered her misquote defence by pointing out it is not close to any real line, because that was something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Nothing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history showing the essay arriving in two large edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on the night of October 28 came close to that night, which is why her answers got shorter there, though it proves nothing about the essay and is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anyone had spoken to Owen before the zero went in, you moved on without answering, so say plainly whether he was asked and offer to hear his account.
